question: Which mass was each GT23 trial divided by, and what factor rescales it to the participant's own mass (D-GT23-C03-1 = B)?

rules.source: GT23-C03 audit tolerance_v2 (fixed there; not recomputed here)
rules.candidate_band_note: about +/-5 %; calibrated on 5 level-walk trials, out of sample worst 4.9 % (3 of 3), so the margin is thin
rules.knee: recorded only (knee-ankle disagreement spans -0.31 to +0.15 log in C03 reliable trials, so it is not a gate)
rules.power_check: ratio of published power to published moment x published joint velocity (deg/s -> rad/s): median of P / (M w) over finite samples with |M w| at or above its 75th percentile (slope and corr also recorded). Shares the moment divisor when |log median ratio| <= the candidate band half width in every tested ANKLE column (a different divisor would scale every column of the trial equally; knee ratios are recorded only, because pilot 2 showed published knee power below M w by 3-17 % in trials whose ankle ratio is 1.00, cause not identified); this detects a different table mass more than about 5 % away (e.g. own vs another subject), not small differences. Revised after pilot 1 (2 subjects): the first rule (|log slope| <= 0.02 and corr >= 0.98) failed on filtering differences between the published velocity and power (knee slopes 0.84-0.99, corr 0.93-0.99). Not a gate for the moment class.

classes.exact: the trial matched by a local N*m re-run whose ankle/knee columns all correlate >= 0.9999 with the published moments; divisor = the README table mass within 0.1 % of the re-run slope
classes.unique-estimate: reliable lever estimate; every README mass inside the band lies within 0.5 % of the others (one mass value); divisor = the nearest such table mass
classes.ambiguous: reliable lever estimate; table masses more than 0.5 % apart lie inside the band
classes.no-match: reliable lever estimate; no README table mass inside the band
classes.unreliable: family outside the reliable locomotion families (non-gait task or curb), fewer than 4 gait stances, ankle corr < 0.98, unequal time bases, or no model in Statics.csv

rules.rescale: rescale_factor = divisor / own README mass, only for exact and unique-estimate; per-kg own-mass value = published x rescale_factor (moments and, if the power check passes, powers)

sensitivity.rule: unique-estimate is fragile when another README mass lies within one calibration robust sd (0.0152 log) outside the band

rules.min_gait_stances_why: Per-stance ankle implied mass in the census (220 trial sides with >= 4 stances) has a robust log sd of 0.020 (median), 0.033 (75th pct) and 0.047 (90th pct). Requiring the pooled estimate's sampling error (sd / sqrt(n)) to be no larger than the C03 calibration robust sd (0.0152 log) for a 90th-percentile trial gives n >= (0.047 / 0.0152)^2 = 9.7, so 10 gait stances (both legs). Matched trials have 4 or >= 11 stances, so any threshold from 5 to 11 gives the same split.
rules.second_estimator: fitted-talus least squares (module docstring); bias = median(D / exact divisor) over the 8 exact trials
rules.agreement: the second estimate (divided by its bias) lies within the C03 band (0.0488 log) of the matched divisor AND the matched mass value is the README table value nearest to it (values within 0.5 % count as one)
rules.fail_action: unique-estimate trials failing either screen are re-classed ambiguous (not rescalable); exact trials are not screened
rules.post_hoc_note: Added after the census and after the verifier showed that short-trial matches depend on the estimator.
